messages:
From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 15:02:00 -0500
Subject: Post-call recap + recommended next steps (model fit & perf profiles)

Thanks again for the 30-minute walkthrough today — really useful to see how FinLytics is using the extraction pipeline and where latency spikes matter for your analyst UI. Quick recap and action items from my side: 

- Goal alignment: reduce tail latency for interactive search sessions (p95 target <= 350ms) while keeping costs within your current budget band.
- Primary eval axis: generation quality on financial table-to-text prompts, hallucination rate on entity extraction, and p50/p95 latency under typical 2k-token context loads.

Recommended models (initial):
- rw-large-v1 (full precision) — best quality for complex table descriptions.
- rw-q4_8k (quantized) — cost-efficient for bulk reranking and short-form generation.

Benchmarks & artifacts I’m sharing: attached prompt set (finlytics_prompt_set_v1.json) and Redwood-verified performance profiles for the recommended variants. Benchmarks show: rw-large-v1 at ~120 TPS (batched) with p50=72ms, p95=340ms under our sample workload; rw-q4_8k at ~220 TPS with p50=38ms, p95=165ms. Full CSV and dashboard links below.

Links:
- Perf profile (rw-large-v1): https://console.redwood.ai/perf/profiles/rw-large-v1
- Raw benchmarks CSV: https://s3.redwood.ai/benchmarks/finlytics-2027-01-16-results.csv
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/98765

Open questions / requests from FinLytics to help us validate fit:
1) Can you share a 5–10 sample prompts (anonymized) and one representative small dataset of typical documents?
2) Are you comfortable with a short A/B eval where rw-q4_8k runs on Dedicated vs. hosted rw-large-v1 as a fallback?

Next steps (proposed):
- Dylan to run a 2-hour smoke benchmark on your sample prompts (if you can share) and return a focused report.
- Schedule a 60-minute technical trial kickoff next week to configure dedicated pool sizing and discuss rollout policy.

If that sounds right I'll: 1) upload a tailored perf dashboard for FinLytics, 2) provision a trial key for the dedicated candidate, and 3) share a short test plan.

Thanks — looking forward to your samples.

Best,

Laura Bennett
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Hi Rajesh / Sofia — Dylan here (solutions engineer). Quick answers and a proposed short plan: 

1) Latency context: the numbers Laura quoted are from hosted benchmark runs that mirror your interactive workload (2k token average). For Dedicated reserved pools we typically see p95 improve ~15–30% depending on instance SKU because of reduced noisy-neighbor variance. For your target of p95 <= 350ms at 250 concurrent users we recommend a Dedicated pool sized for ~200–250 concurrent model workers (we'll show exact sizing after we run a smoke benchmark on your prompts).

2) Quality/regression monitoring: Redwood Optimize has a lightweight eval harness we can attach to your prompt set — it tracks per-prompt quality (BLEU/ROUGE when applicable), hallucination indicators, and can alert on regressions vs a baseline prompt set. We maintain per-release model profiles and flag known regressions; I attached the short runbook in the dashboard under "Regression Checks".

Proposed technical trial plan (2 steps):
- Step A (today/48hrs): you share 20 anonymized prompts + 200 sample rows; we run a 2-hour smoke benchmark and provide a focused table with TPS, p50/p95, and quality delta vs rw-large-v1 baseline.
- Step B (1 week): small canary on Dedicated: rw-q4_8k in production path with rw-large-v1 fallback for long-form; collect quality signals and cost numbers for one week.

Deliverables: smoke benchmark CSV, Redwood perf profile link for the trial models, short test plan, and a recommended pool sizing doc.

Can you confirm you’ll upload the samples to the shared S3 link (we’ll send a presigned URL) and whether FinLytics legal needs an NDA before we run the trial?

Cheers,

Dylan Brooks
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
